name: Biberwier
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful village at the Fernpass with the natural bathing lake Badesee Biberwier and access to the Zugspitzarena.
beschreibung:
Overview

Biberwier is a historic municipality in the Reutte district of Tyrol's Außerfern region, situated at around 989 meters above sea level at the southern edge of the Lermoos basin. Home to roughly 650 residents, this sun-drenched village nestles directly at the northern base of the Fern Pass, framed by the striking Ehrwalder Sonnenspitze peak of the Mieming Chain to the east and the Lechtal Alps to the west. Within the municipal borders lie the crystal-clear Loisach River springs and a chain of pristine mountain lakes formed by a massive prehistoric rockslide: Blindsee, Mittersee, and Weißensee. Biberwier enchants visitors with its rich mining history, outstanding family recreation at the Marienberg lifts, and its premier setting in the Tiroler Zugspitz Arena.

History

Human activity here has been linked to the Fern Pass since antiquity, when the Roman emperor Claudius developed the vital Via Claudia Augusta trade highway around 46 AD. Biberwier was first documented in 1287 as Piberwure. The name combines beaver with the Middle High German word wuore (dam or weir), honoring the native beaver colonies that once inhabited the Loisach marshes. Beginning in the mid-15th century, the village achieved fame as a thriving mining center on the Silberleithe mountain. Over centuries, miners extracted silver, lead, and zinc, carving out an astonishing subterranean tunnel network stretching 59 kilometers. Large-scale extraction flourished through the 18th century before ending in the 1920s. The Neoclassical parish church dedicated to Saint Joseph was constructed between 1827 and 1831, standing under historic protection alongside the preserved mining monuments.

How to Get There

By car, Biberwier is directly accessible via the Fernpass federal highway B179. From Germany, motorists can travel toll- and vignette-free via Füssen/Reutte or through Garmisch-Partenkirchen and Ehrwald. From the Inn Valley, access is via Nassereith across the crest of the Fern Pass into the village. Rail travelers take the Außerfern Railway to the nearby stations of Lermoos or Ehrwald, situated only three kilometers away. Frequent regional VVT buses and guest shuttles provide direct connections to Biberwier.

Tips

A premier summer attraction is the Marienberg lift system, featuring the longest summer toboggan run in Tyrol, hurtling down 1,300 meters through forty banked turns from the middle station at 1,180 meters, complemented by downhill monster roller and mountain cart tracks. Along the Silberleithe Mining Trail, 25 interpretive panels, historic mine adits, and an authentic gunpowder house reveal the dramatic lives of historic miners. The Three Lakes Hike connects the turquoise waters of Lake Blindsee, Lake Mittersee, and Lake Weißensee, with the 30-meter-deep Blindsee ranking among the top scuba diving lakes in the Alps. Winter brings sunny family skiing at Marienberg and instant access to the Nordic skiing trails of the Lermoos basin.
